object_description: square flat structure with a horizontal tripartite division and two covered inner courtyards
geometry_property: large footprint set by the hall length
structural dichotomy expressed in the facade
design_condition: the square flat volume sits along the street so that a generous outdoor space opens towards the sports centre, its footprint dictated by the length of the sports hall

positive: The square flat structure creates a generous outdoor space towards the sports centre
The classic horizontal tripartite division structures the building well and harmoniously
The structural dichotomy is strongly reflected in the facade
The well-functioning cluster units are arranged in a quarter of the floor plan each around the two courtyards
It seems possible to illuminate the rooms arranged around them
Canteen and communal spaces sit as a piano nobile on the extra-high floor with access to the courtyards
The narrow access layer is the structural backbone dividing the building in two
Usable areas are only to be separated by non-load-bearing walls
The building volume is basically compact with a good cost-benefit ratio
The chosen structure provides a very high degree of long-term flexibility
The outdoor space integrates the school grounds harmoniously and transparently into the surroundings
An open green belt of meadow with freely arranged trees creates zones and vistas
Connecting the playing field to the green space creates a generous contiguous open area
The all-weather pitch and sports facilities are cleverly connected to the break area
The terraced school garden is well positioned in relation to the family gardens
The project impresses with its stringent, conceptual approach
negative: At first glance the floor plan dimensions seem to dominate the site
The placement of certain ancillary rooms along the internal street is incomprehensible
The communal rooms on the raised floor have no direct ground-level connection to the outside
The concrete slats are potentially expensive to produce and generate unusable room heights
The structural feasibility of the slat to outer wall connections remains an open question
The fragmented central schoolyard with its double path and stairs is unresolved
The character of the building is perceived as off-putting and too autonomous
Whether the chosen expression meets the requirements of an elementary school is questioned
Access via the ramp is very narrow and contradicts the idea of a school for small children
The sparse plan material and reduced model make the project difficult to understand
